properties.name: Yetholme Sunset Overlook
properties.notes:
Located in the high-altitude Central Tablelands, this spot offers expansive views of the horizon. It is a popular stop for motorists looking to capture their vehicles against dramatic, unobstructed sunset skies and rolling silhouettes.
— @dylan660, https://atlasphoto.app/post/b3548e60-526b-4e8d-b6b5-4a9f414d10d0

properties.name: Mount Panorama Pit Lane
properties.notes:
Located at the iconic Mount Panorama Circuit, the pit lane offers a professional automotive backdrop. The numbered garage doors and industrial textures provide a clean, repetitive pattern that complements vehicle lines, making it a premier spot for car photography.
— @chubcars, https://atlasphoto.app/post/ca3e92ec-4818-4707-b6b8-4ad1eb32bea7

properties.name: Bathurst Chase Parking Garage
properties.notes:
A spacious indoor parking structure in central Bathurst, providing a minimalist industrial setting for automotive photography. The grid of pillars and artificial lighting offer great opportunities for framing and light play on vehicles.
— @pete82, https://atlasphoto.app/post/9b8955c2-4742-4744-b3b5-9c453f9453c2

properties.name: Bathurst Self-Service Car Wash
properties.notes:
A practical location for automotive enthusiasts to capture clean detail shots. The artificial lighting of the wash bays at night provides high-contrast illumination, perfect for highlighting metallic textures and water reflections on vehicles.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/32a5b5e0-7ff1-4370-8bf8-db23e1b0577d

properties.name: Bathurst Showground
properties.notes:

— @vannnnah, https://atlasphoto.app/post/e1f43a7d-7136-406d-a5fe-ec2271cf0fa6

properties.name: Bathurst Indoor Sports Stadium
properties.notes:

— https://atlasphoto.app/post/93938435-c7ae-410c-8a23-ae387125a0e5

properties.name: Kelso Garden Sunset
properties.notes:
A peaceful suburban garden setting in Kelso, offering clear views of the horizon for sunset photography. The open space allows for capturing dramatic sky textures and golden hour light over local flora and garden structures.
— @vannnnah, https://atlasphoto.app/post/7137287a-e5da-4a4d-bca1-8d9fd7c2d3ae

properties.name: The Esses
properties.notes:
The Esses are the flowing, elevation-change sweepers on Mount Panorama near Bathurst — a prime spot for capturing high-speed racing lines, dramatic car lean and dynamic compositions against the hills. Visit during race weekends (Bathurst 1000) for peak action and atmosphere; for cleaner light and fewer crowds choose early morning or late afternoon golden hour. Accessibility: public viewing areas and official grandstands; track is closed to traffic during events and open for limited public access
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/9cce2ce1-1f66-445a-894b-cdf9496f38ff

properties.name: John Hinxman Vista
properties.notes:
High vantage overlooking the legendary Mount Panorama circuit — sweeping curves, elevation changes and surrounding Blue Mountains make striking compositions. Best at sunrise or golden hour for warm side-light and long shadows; evening can produce dramatic skies. Accessible by car with small lookout parking; no entry fee but expect crowds during race events (Bathurst 1000). Paths and railings limit angles; bring layers (windy, changeable weather).
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/6e54622a-6e3f-4a12-bb3f-b9e15105fdc8

properties.name: Abercrombie House
properties.notes:
Victorian Italianate mansion set in formal gardens — rich interiors, ornate facades, and mature trees provide varied compositions. Best at golden hour for warm light on the sandstone and long shadows; autumn and late-spring gardens add colour. House operates as a museum with guided tours and seasonal events—check opening hours and entry fees. On-site parking; narrow paths and interior stairs limit accessibility. Respect signs and preservation rules when shooting inside.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/b82f5f50-2a3c-4b7b-a45c-550f50d05efb

properties.name: Bathurst Begonia House & Fernery
properties.notes:
A compact Victorian-style glasshouse and fernery showcasing vibrant begonias, trailing ferns and textured foliage—ideal for close-up color studies and sheltered architectural frames. Visit weekday mornings or late afternoon for soft, directional light; overcast days yield even color. Small site with paved paths and limited parking on Court House Ln; casual entry (check seasonal opening hours). Respect plant signs and avoid flash to protect blooms. Special for intimate botanical detail and the mo
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/ae649f97-c05e-4f23-a6fa-509b0b18dd94

properties.name: Australian Fossil and Mineral Museum
properties.notes:
Compact museum housing an extensive collection of fossils and minerals — opals, marine fossils, dinosaur remains and polished specimens. Shoot dramatic textures, colors and small-scale detail under controlled gallery lighting. Best on weekday mornings to avoid crowds; check the museum's photography policy (tripods/flash often prohibited). Easily reached by car from Bathurst; on-site parking nearby. Low-light interior favors fast lenses and higher ISO.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/5da5b4a7-052a-476e-ab7a-57c190dee318

properties.name: Kings Parade
properties.notes:
Kings Parade in Bathurst offers a classic regional parade route and streetscape—good for event, street and civic architecture photos. Photograph marching bands, community events, tree-lined avenues and heritage facades. Best at golden hour or during scheduled civic parades and ANZAC services for dramatic light and atmosphere. Easily accessible by car with street parking and nearby public parking in Bathurst CBD; check local event calendars for closures. No special entry requirements.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/b1786f6d-3639-41f9-ba81-029c7ef43368

properties.name: Bathurst War Memorial Carillon
properties.notes:
A limestone carillon and WWI/WWII memorial set on a hill with a slim tower, sculpted stonework and sweeping views over Bathurst valley. Photograph architectural details (pews, plaques, bells), framed tower silhouettes at sunrise/sunset, and wide panoramas from the viewing platform. Best light: golden hour and blue hour for dramatic skies; ANZAC Day and memorial services add emotive human moments. Site is car-accessible with nearby street parking; check opening hours and guided-tour times before訪
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/93f0918a-8ed0-43b4-b955-a44ff03b66b1

properties.name: National Motor Racing Museum
properties.notes:
Historic race cars, trophies and interactive exhibits provide tight detail and dramatic wide shots; combine museum interiors with panoramic exterior views of the nearby Mount Panorama circuit. Best visited weekdays or early morning for soft light and few visitors; golden hour on the nearby track yields warm low-angle light. Museum has paid entry, wheelchair access and on-site parking; allow 1–2 hours. Combine interior close-ups with context shots of the hilltop circuit and grandstands.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/4f10f8fd-32b4-4705-89cc-5ebd04767594

properties.name: Turon State Forest
properties.notes:
Turon State Forest offers rugged eucalypt ridges, river corridors and scattered rocky outcrops — ideal for moody landscape shots, intimate forest scenes and birdlife. Best light is at sunrise or late afternoon; spring brings wildflowers, autumn cooler tones. Access is via Eskdale Rd with informal parking near trailheads; expect unsealed roads and limited facilities — a high-clearance vehicle helps. No entry fee but follow signage and biosecurity rules. Less crowded than national parks, it’s good
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/a7a1d38e-0ea1-4ed5-95e1-755cae26389f

properties.name: Miss Traill's House
properties.notes:
Miss Traill's House is a compact 19th‑century heritage home and museum on Russell St — valuable for photographing intact Victorian interiors, decorative timberwork, leadlight windows, a timber verandah and a small heritage garden. Best visited at golden hour for warm exterior light; weekday mornings avoid tours and school groups. Interiors may have restricted tripods and flash — check opening hours and entry fees with the museum. Street parking and short walk from central Bathurst; expect tight,

properties.name: Centennial Park Bathurst
properties.notes:
A compact civic park with mature trees, formal garden beds, heritage monuments and paved paths — good for intimate landscapes, environmental portraits and detail shots of memorial architecture and seasonal plantings. Visit at golden hour for warm light through tree canopies; weekday mornings are quieter. Easy street parking on Seymour/Rocket St, flat accessible paths, no entry fee. Local events (ANZAC services, markets) provide candid moments and flags/ceremonial setups.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/86c3f353-9c69-4933-95e1-6877286580e4

properties.name: Chifley Home and Education Centre
properties.notes:
A well-preserved 19th-century terrace where Prime Minister Ben Chifley lived — shoot evocative period interiors, original furnishings, exterior façade and small cottage garden. Best light is morning or late afternoon for warm side-light on façade and textured interiors. Entry is via guided tour; check opening hours and photography rules (flash often restricted). On-street parking on Busby St; site is compact with narrow rooms and limited tripod space. Cultural context: an intimate slice of mid-‑
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/8132f19d-a86a-4235-8dd2-b007a453ec92

properties.name: Machattie Park
properties.notes:
Machattie Park is a manicured Victorian-era town park in central Bathurst with formal gardens, a central fountain/rotunda, mature trees and seasonal flower beds — great for garden details, architectural shots of the rotunda and relaxed street-park compositions. Visit early morning or late afternoon for soft light and few people. Easily walkable from Bathurst CBD; street parking and nearby car parks; wheelchair-accessible paths. No entry fee; check for events (markets, ANZAC services) that add a촏

properties.name: Bathurst War Memorial
properties.notes:
A compact, formal World War I memorial set in a parked boulevard on Russell Street — photogenic for stoic sculptures, inscriptions and symmetrical approaches framed by mature plane trees. Best at golden hour for warm side-light and long shadows; ANZAC Day and Remembrance services offer atmospheric crowd and ceremonial moments. Public park access, no entry fee; street parking and small car parks nearby. Weekday mornings are quieter; watch for event closures during ceremonies.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/700d6927-8c67-488d-8888-9334cf9ad11b

properties.name: The Bridle Track Start
properties.notes:
A trailhead into Newnes Plateau–style bushland: photograph the Bridle Track corridor from the start, leading lines through eucalypt scrub, and textured sandstone/leaf litter in changing light. Expect misty mornings and soft shade; conditions can shift fast in the Blue Mountains hinterland. Access is by car to nearby trail parking; no permits typically, but check local trail status and park alerts.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/f390d1a3-569c-4041-b1fb-2ed0de1d3ab4

properties.name: Boundary Road Reserve
properties.notes:
Small local reserve with open paddocks, scattered eucalypts and winding walking tracks — good for intimate landscape and nature studies, seasonal colour and cloudscapes. Best at golden hour or after rain for saturated colours; easy roadside parking and level paths make access simple. No entry fees; respect local residents and dog-leash rules. Great for quiet sunrise/sunset silhouettes and close-up bark/seed pod textures.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/d69956f3-ef20-45e6-a279-7416d1131971

properties.name: Extreme Flying Fox
properties.notes:
A commercial flying-fox/zipline experience over bushland near Bathurst—great for dynamic action shots of riders suspended above trees and valley, plus environmental wide angles showing scale. Visit golden hour for warm side light and long shadows; overcast days work for even skin tones. Book sessions in advance; operator safety briefings are required. Site is car-accessible with limited parking—arrive 20–30 minutes early. Weekdays have fewer families than weekends.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/29868969-8a2e-4568-9a02-8400e4ce4156

properties.name: Bathurst Adventure Playground
properties.notes:
A colorful community playground in central Bathurst offering sculptural play equipment, climbing frames, swings and shady trees — great for environmental portraits, kid-in-action shots and detail textures (rubber surfacing, timber). Easy street parking nearby, no entry fee. Best light: golden hour or soft overcast; weekdays or early mornings for fewer families. Accessible paths and seating make logistics simple; capture candid community life and contrast of play structures against Bathurst's low
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/e4a1ca91-4981-46a1-adc4-0e72bcb86794

properties.name: George Evans Expedition Statue
properties.notes:
A civic bronze statue of explorer George Evans set in Bathurst’s public space — good for documentary and historical portraits with strong sculptural lines and contextual townscape. Visit at golden hour or overcast midday for even tones. Easily accessible on foot from central Bathurst; roadside parking and short walks from nearby car parks. No entry fees; respectful framing around nearby civic buildings and passersby. Best in calm weather or after rain for richer textures on bronze and pavements.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/e2ffe1a7-0a2d-4a42-9fd9-4e83e355f921

properties.name: Pensilvania STATE FOREST
properties.notes:
Pensilvania State Forest near Colo offers quiet bushland scenery: misty gullies, tall eucalypts, winding tracks, and creek-side pockets—ideal for moody landscape frames and woodland textures. Visit after rain for richer greens and low cloud, with daylight filtering through canopy. Entry is generally free; access is via local roads and trailheads—check NSW NPWS updates before driving.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/c9db8c0a-260a-4726-b03e-e03953c7766a

properties.name: Victoria Park
properties.notes:
Victoria Park in Bathurst is a leafy municipal park with open lawns, mature trees and walking paths — good for relaxed landscape, environmental portrait and seasonal shots. Visit at golden hour or after rain for saturated colors; autumn brings warm tones. Easily accessible with street parking and paved paths; no entry fee. Weekday mornings are quieter. Nearby Bathurst heritage streets add context for combined shoots.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/b58f3b7d-1e72-41cc-ae8e-ef759f6f01d6

properties.name: Mount Testa Campgrounds
properties.notes:
Mount Testa Campgrounds suits landscape and nature shots with escarpment-and-valley atmospheres, woodland textures, and calm campfire-night skies. Best light comes at sunrise and sunset; overcast days add soft, contrasty cloud layers. Access is via 613 Messners Rd; parking is at/near the campground—confirm local entry/camping rules and any fire bans before arriving.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/6a280d23-675b-4e11-a0f9-8e0d9cf13f66

properties.name: Pennsylvania State Forest
properties.notes:
Pennsylvania State Forest offers quiet bush tracks, layered eucalyptus canopy, and creek/forest-floor textures—ideal for moody landscape and nature compositions. Best light is early morning (soft rays, lower haze) or late afternoon (warm edge-light through branches). Expect variable weather; bugs can be heavy in warmer months. Access is via local roads/trackheads; parking is typically roadside or at nearby trail starts—carry water, a map/offline GPS, and check NSW forestry/NPWS conditions before
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/03ecf8cd-01df-4727-aae1-33264124eb70

properties.name: The Big Dog
properties.notes:
The Big Dog is a quirky roadside landmark outside Dunkeld, ideal for bold scale shots and storytelling compositions. Photograph it straight-on for the iconic shape, or frame it with the nearby highway/trees for context. Best light is late afternoon to sunset; weekdays reduce passing traffic. Access is usually easy by car, but conditions depend on local road/shoulder safety—park carefully and shoot from safe spots.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/226e2e5d-893f-4e56-a24a-f1a36e38974b

properties.name: Hadiqa-e-Ahmad (Garden of Ahmad)
properties.notes:
Hadiqa-e-Ahmad is a tranquil Islamic garden where symmetry, shaded paths, and framed water/plant details suit calm landscape and architectural-style compositions. Visit on clear mornings for soft, low-angle light and cooler conditions; weekdays are usually quieter. Photographers can roam on foot—bring a tripod if the grounds allow calm, static scenes. Parking is at/near the site along Limekilns Rd.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/1b756480-25da-4777-97d0-0ca16f29385a

properties.name: Sunny corner War memorial
properties.notes:
Sunny Corner War Memorial in NSW offers a quiet, small-scale historical focal point ideal for memorial portraits and respectful landscape compositions. Visit on clear mornings for soft side light across the monument setting; evenings provide warm sky tones over the surrounding countryside. Expect limited services—bring water and plan simple parking near the site.
— https://atlasphoto.app/post/b26c4a68-9d79-4431-9cb5-91d6594f7434

properties.name: Meadow Flat Poplar Row
properties.notes:
This scenic stretch of the Great Western Highway is renowned for its towering rows of poplar trees. During the autumn months, the foliage turns a brilliant golden yellow, creating a spectacular natural corridor that is perfect for automotive and landscape photography.
— @z_hachi, https://atlasphoto.app/post/73816d22-38d0-4857-b7da-866375e00e1f

properties.name: Marrangaroo Lakeside Garden
properties.notes:
This serene spot features a vibrant Japanese Maple overlooking a calm pond. The area is particularly stunning in autumn when the foliage turns deep red, offering excellent opportunities for backlit nature shots and reflections on the water.
— @billan, https://atlasphoto.app/post/e7721bc7-b8c5-45ca-8eea-caaa12a55b51

properties.name: Hassans Walls Lookout
properties.notes:

— https://atlasphoto.app/post/1878acd6-5b95-41ef-bcd9-4dd66f88c025

properties.name: The Foundations Portland
properties.notes:
A historic industrial site featuring the skeletal remains of the Portland Cement Works. The rusted steel frames and weathered concrete provide striking geometric patterns and textures, set against the natural backdrop of the New South Wales bushland.
— @vannnnah, https://atlasphoto.app/post/9feaac1f-8b93-4b32-8178-10a18732592e

properties.name: Wolgan Valley Night Overlook
properties.notes:
Wolgan Valley is renowned for its dramatic sandstone escarpments and exceptionally dark skies, providing a perfect canvas for astrophotography and capturing celestial events far from urban light pollution.
— @jt_beam3r, https://atlasphoto.app/post/7d07bb83-6d3a-4ec0-8791-41a8e43b599d

properties.name: Rydal Bushland Retreat
properties.notes:
A serene spot in the Australian bush, offering moody views of eucalyptus forests. The location is perfect for capturing atmospheric, low-light scenes that blend architectural comfort with wild nature.
— @kyle0, https://atlasphoto.app/post/b57b48d3-ef59-4eec-85f1-73bda1f48a8b

properties.name: Mugii Murum-Ban State Conservation Area
properties.notes:

Photograph panoramic cliff vistas, mist-filled valleys at dawn, and long-exposure falls after rain. Best at sunrise or golden hour for directional light and at dusk for warm cliff tones; post-rain days reveal cascades. Most lookouts have short, well-marked trails and roadside parking with no entry fee—arrive early on weekdays to avoid crowds. Trails can be wet

properties.notes:

Shoot wide panoramas from lookouts at sunrise/sunset for warm side-light on textured cliffs; overcast days reveal subtle rock detail and vertical forms. Access is via sealed roads to several parking areas and short walks; some trails and pagoda areas require decent footwear and moderate scrambling. No entry fee; respect signage and traditional custodians.冬

Best at sunrise for soft light and possible fog filling the valley, or at golden-hour sunset for warm side-light on cliffs. Access is via unsealed roads off Glen Alice; a high-clearance vehicle is recommended and expect basic parking at the lookout. Shoot sweeping panoramas from the highest knobs at sunrise or sunset for warm sidelighting and long shadows. Accessible via a short walk from a roadside parking area; no facilities, limited signage, and no entry fee. Weekday mornings have fewer visitors. Winter mornings offer crisp air and clear visibility; spring adds wildflowers.

Elevated roadside lookout offering sweeping views of a patchwork valley, rolling hills and distant ranges — ideal for wide panoramas, layered landscapes and moody skies. Best at golden hour (sunrise or sunset) when low light sculpts ridgelines; blue hour brings long-exposure mood. Accessible by car on Brogans Creek road; limited parking on-site and short walk to the rail. No entry fees. Expect variable weather; weekdays are quieter. Respect private farmland boundaries.

properties.name: Mugii Dhudungura

properties.name: Ultimate Slot
properties.notes:

Best at sunrise or late afternoon when side-light reveals textures; mid-winter low sun increases shafts. Remote access—expect unsealed roads and a short walk from parking; use 4WD if wet. No formal entry point; respect private land signs and stay on tracks. Minimal crowds make it great for longer shoots.

properties.notes:
